name: AGC homepage: Associated General Contractors of America trade body site
title: AGC homepage: Associated General Contractors of America trade body site
answer: This is the homepage of the Associated General Contractors of America, a US construction trade association with over 27,000 member firms. It is mostly a landing page for events, courses and a heavy civil platform, so it offers little direct AI content. Its most useful items are news headlines: construction input costs rose 8.9% between August 2025 and August 2026, and an association survey found war and tariff impacts disrupting projects. It also reports contractors added 22,000 jobs in August and unemployment hit a record low 3.1%.

sections.body: The Associated General Contractors of America publishes this page on agc.org. It is the association's homepage, not a research report or a technology adoption study. It presents AGC as a trade body with over 27,000 member firms and lists services for members, events, a leadership course and a connected platform for heavy civil and infrastructure work. The page carries no publication date. The supplied text was harvested on 26 September 2026.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page opens with an invitation to construction safety professionals to meet in San Diego to exchange ideas, build relationships and bring proven solutions back to their teams. It advertises AGC's Leadership for Project Executives Course, described as preparing aspiring and newly appointed project executives to step confidently into complex, high impact responsibilities of executive level project leadership. It also promotes one connected platform for winning, planning and managing heavy civil and infrastructure work, from the first estimate to the final report. AGC describes itself as having over 27,000 member firms and providing a full range of services that satisfy members' needs and concerns, improve the quality of construction and protect the public interest. The page then lists two news headlines. The first says construction input costs climbed 8.9% between August 2025 and August 2026, and that an association survey found war and tariff impacts are disrupting projects. The second says contractors added 22,000 jobs in August, the construction unemployment rate hit a record low of 3.1%, and an association survey found firms struggle to fill openings. The page gives no further detail on these surveys or on technology adoption.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: AGC states it has over 27,000 member firms. It reports construction input costs climbed 8.9% between August 2025 and August 2026. It reports contractors added 22,000 jobs in August and the construction unemployment rate hit a record low of 3.1%. It says an association survey found war and tariff impacts disrupting projects, and another survey finding firms struggle to fill openings. It gives no definition of AI or technology adoption.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in construction would find little direct AI material here. The page is useful as a signpost to AGC's survey headlines on costs, tariffs, war impacts, hiring and unemployment, which give market context. It does not provide AI adoption figures, safety technology compliance data or survey methodology, so it cannot support claims about AI use in construction on its own.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Construction

sections.body: This is a homepage and promotional landing page, not a report. It does not cover AI, technology adoption rates, safety technology compliance or survey methods. It gives no publication date, and the news headlines lack article links or detail in the supplied text. The only date stated is the harvest date, 26 September 2026, while the headlines refer to August 2025 to August 2026 and August jobs data. It is partial and commercial in purpose, promoting AGC events, courses and a platform.
